summary: Copper metal films were grown on oxide substrates using copper (I) chloride, water, and hydrogen as precursors. The study compared two deposition schemes: one with water and one without. The addition of water increased the growth rate on alumina substrates but decreased it on silica substrates. The process involved sequential oxidation and reduction steps, with hydrogen reducing the oxide layer to copper metal. The films showed polycrystalline structures with varying textures depending on the substrate orientation.
evidence: Films of copper metal have been grown on two different oxide substrate materials by atomic layer deposition. The film depositions were carried out in the temperature range 375–475 8C. Copper (I) chloride, water and hydrogen were used as precursors. Two deposition schemes were used and compared, one including water (CuClyHO yH ) and another without water22 (CuClyH ).
